h: Know before you bowl in Digbeth
p: Digbeth is a short walk from Birmingham Moor Street station and not far from New Street either, so it's an easy one to reach by train. That's handy, because a night here can easily stretch on once the drinks and games get going. Bring photo ID if you look anywhere near young, as bar-led venues commonly check, and it saves an awkward moment at the door.

If you're organising for a group, think about numbers before you book. A few friends can share one lane comfortably, while a bigger party might want two lanes side by side so everyone gets enough turns. Mixing bowling with whatever bar games are on that night is a good way to keep the whole group busy, and swapping teams halfway through stops one person dominating the scoreboard.

Digbeth itself has a lively personality. It's long been the heart of Birmingham's Irish community, and the city's big St Patrick's Day parade has traditionally made its way through the area each March, bringing huge crowds and plenty of craic. The old canals around Warwick Bar give a glimpse of Birmingham's industrial past, and you'll find lots of former factories reinvented as studios, venues and bars.

Gig fans will find music venues nearby too, so it's easy to make a full night of it: a few frames of bowling, a bite to eat, then on to a show. Just keep an eye on the time if you've got a last train to catch.
